title: the uk is putting up to £23m behind safe, evidence-based AI and
description: Why evidence-based AI and edtech trials need measurable outcomes and safety controls before schools adopt them.
tldr: the uk putting up to £23m behind safe, evidence-based AI and edtech trials in schools is a clear signal. novelty gets attention, while measurable outcomes and safety controls help regulated buyers move toward adoption.

sections.h2: what is the uk funding telling builders about school AI?
body: the uk is putting up to £23m behind safe, evidence-based AI and edtech trials in schools. that is the signal: school adoption is being shaped around evidence and safety.
for builders, the path into regulated education buyers runs through measurable outcomes and safety controls.

sections.h2: why do regulated buyers want evidence before adoption?
body: regulated buyers want measurable outcomes and safety controls before adoption. the requirement is tied to whether a product can show results and operate safely in a school setting.
that changes the conversation around AI and edtech from interest in what is new to confidence in what has been tested.

sections.h2: does novelty still matter when selling AI to schools?
body: novelty gets you noticed. it can create initial attention around a product or trial.
evidence gets you through the door. measurable outcomes and safety controls give regulated buyers the basis for adoption.

sections.h2: what should solo builders take from this funding signal?
body: the transferable lesson is direct: build for evidence and safety alongside the product itself. a novel idea may start the conversation, while proof and controls support the next conversation with a regulated buyer.
the funding signal points toward AI and edtech trials where outcomes can be measured and safety can be addressed clearly.
